# Guild routing

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-skill-docs.py from docs/reference/skills.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

For what each skill reads and writes, see the [skills reference](reference/skills.md). This file maps each `/crav1-…` skill and `*-agent` subagent to a lane — Specify, Plan, Build, or Cross-cutting — and records cross-cutting helpers, so a kit consumer can route work when the kit changes. Cross-cutting skills may be invoked from any phase, and cross-cutting helpers may be flagged from any phase. Neither is owned by Specify, Plan, or Build alone, and neither by itself moves work into another lane.

Kit source of truth: [https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit](https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit).

Skill slash names are `/crav1-…`. Subagent names end in `-agent`.

## Starter options

When the user asks for startup options, these six are the only ways in. That ask names the list. It does not run a skill. It does not move work into a lane. Each starter still follows the rules it already has. Every other skill is a later skill.

| Starter | Runs when |
| --- | --- |
| `/crav1-spark-to-spec` | The user brings one or two sentences |
| `/crav1-ideas-to-spec` | The user brings a pile of ideas and technical hunches |
| `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` | The user brings mixed files, or more than one v0 feature |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | The user names existing repos, with or without a dump to match |
| `/crav1-read-environment` | The user names the host |
| `/crav1-fix-bug` | The user names a real bug |

The same list is where a lone user sees the ways to start: [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md) and [first-run.md](first-run.md).

## Specify

| Kind | Name |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | `/crav1-spark-to-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-ideas-to-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` |
| Skill | `/crav1-review-architecture` |
| Skill | `/crav1-tighten-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` |
| Subagent | `crav1-spec-reviewer-agent` |
| Subagent | `crav1-review-architecture-agent` |
| Subagent | `crav1-bundle-slice-agent` |

`/crav1-tighten-spec` tightens the picked issue in an existing spec. The user calls it. It calls no skill. It does not rewrite the spec to match the code, and it does not clear a stale research mark.

`/crav1-resolve-open-questions` settles open questions and **Conflict:** lines. Nothing is written until one confirm. `/crav1-add-to-spec` and `/crav1-finalize-commit` name it when they write a Conflict line, and do not run it.

A guided walk from a draft spec through the plan until ready to build is `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build` (1.119.0). It is cross-cutting, so neither Specify nor Plan owns it. It runs the Specify skills this lane already owns, inside the walk, and does not replace them. It does not start Build. The new-slice route is unchanged. Architecture review stays optional on that route. Inside the walk it always runs.

`/crav1-add-to-spec`, `/crav1-bundle-to-specs`, and `/crav1-existing-to-specs` follow the imported-sources check when they quote an imported source. Secrets are always redacted. The check may write the transfer data policy after a yes and never writes a secrets choice. `/crav1-add-to-spec` writes `docs/notes/` on Note, `Used by <slug>` when a spec quotes a note, and `Absorbed by <slug>` only after a yes. `/crav1-spark-to-spec`, `/crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `/crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `/crav1-existing-to-specs`, and `/crav1-tighten-spec` do the same when they quote a note. They do not commit. The check is `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/sources.md`.

After a quote is kept, `/crav1-add-to-spec` compares it with `docs/research/` through its fact branch and does not run that check a second time. The mark is written only after a yes. It drafts a revisit and does not send it. `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` and `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` clear or narrow the mark and do not commit. The wording is `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/research-stale.md`.

## Plan

| Kind | Name |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | `/crav1-plan-from-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-review-plan` |
| Skill | `/crav1-tighten-plan` |
| Subagent | `crav1-plan-reviewer-agent` |

`/crav1-plan-from-spec` writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md` from the accepted spec. The user calls it. It calls no skill. It stops before Build when `## Linter` says there is no linter, until the user chooses. A piece the user leaves is not turned into work on a later run unless the user says so.

`/crav1-review-plan` reads the plan and writes nothing. The user calls it. It calls no skill. It names `/crav1-tighten-plan` and does not run it.

The same walk, `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build`, runs `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, then `/crav1-review-plan` and `/crav1-tighten-plan`, then the ready check. It does not replace those skills. It stops when the check is clear and does not start `/crav1-build-tasks`. When the slice is ready, or ready-partial with tasks that can start, the ending recommends `/crav1-build-walk` and names `/crav1-build-tasks` as the alternative for one task without the walk. Since 1.150.0 that recommendation is a Run next block first, and each command is a complete invocation for a new session.

## Build

| Kind | Name |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | `/crav1-build-tasks` |
| Skill | `/crav1-build-features` |
| Skill | `/crav1-build-walk` |
| Skill | `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` |
| Subagent | `crav1-build-task-agent` |

`/crav1-build-walk` is in the Build lane. The user asks for the walk. It opens the build, verify, commit, and pull-request skills by file and does not replace them. The reply prints Run next first, one complete command per branch that can start, and a step skill's own Next is not printed. Recording a step commits the progress file and does not push. It does not push, open, or merge without a yes in that run. It never rebases.

Started from a ready-to-build report, the walk offers each ready branch as its own Next, with the T number beside the task name. A task that needs code from an unmerged branch is cut from that branch, and the merge list says the order back. Other-owner mode never opens a pull request and never merges.

`/crav1-existing-to-specs` is a starter option. Asking for startup options names it and does not run it. It may run from any lane, and only when the user names repos. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not `/crav1-add-to-spec`.

`/crav1-existing-to-specs recheck` (also `repos vs specs`) may run from any lane once specs exist. It writes nothing into any spec and never an open question. A gap goes to `/crav1-add-to-spec` only after a yes. A new feature is named, not started.

`/crav1-read-environment` is a starter option. Asking for startup options names it and does not run it. It may run from any lane, and only when the user names the host. Naming production, prod, or live stops. It never reads production data. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. Confirmed system facts go through `/crav1-refresh-system-notes`, architecture facts through `/crav1-existing-to-specs`, and a slice Match through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. It asks once whether to run `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` and does not run that refresh from the question.

`/crav1-fix-bug` is a starter option. Asking for startup options names it and does not run it. It may run from any lane, and only when the user names a real bug. It names the lane and does not move work into it or start it. A spec miss goes to Specify, a plan miss to Plan, and a verify miss or a broken implementation to Build. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. When the bug changes how the parts connect, it asks once whether to run `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` and does not run it.

`/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` may run from any lane when the user names a person, one spec, a topic, a branch, or a pull request. Nothing is sent. `/crav1-add-to-spec` links answers back. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-record-approval` may run from any lane. It records a named person's yes on an Approval needed item and does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. Plan and Build create the item, and the yes is recorded whenever it arrives. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-add-to-spec` may run from any lane. If there is no pointer, it stops and asks. A kept new feature names `/crav1-spark-to-spec`, `/crav1-ideas-to-spec`, or `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` and does not run it. A kept bug names `/crav1-fix-bug` and does not run it. It does not commit, does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build, and does not start those lanes. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-review-pr` may run from any lane, and only when the user names an open pull request in that turn. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It only names the lane for a finding. It names `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` after that pull request merges and does not run it. Spark, specify, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-pr-status` may run from any lane, and only when the user names a pull request in that turn, or the current branch has exactly one open pull request. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It hands spec or decision points to `/crav1-add-to-spec` on a yes and follow-ups to `/crav1-ado-sync` as drafts. It never posts.

`/crav1-merge-pr` may run from any lane, and only when the user explicitly asks in that turn to merge a named pull request. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-help` may run from any lane. It answers what to run next, in what order, and what a skill does, from the kit's own docs, never GitHub. It writes nothing and runs no skill. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Agents call it before they suggest more than one next step.

`/crav1-update-kit` may run from any lane when the user asks to update the installed kit. Optional `to vX.Y.Z`. The default is the latest published release tag. It refuses `main`, a branch, a commit, and an open pull request. It does not switch branches and never rebases. A yes from an agent does not write. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` may run from any lane, any time, when you type it. It is command-only. It names `/crav1-build-tasks` and does not run it. It does not move work into Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-explain-existing-system` may run from any lane. It reads `docs/system/` and writes nothing. It names `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` or `/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this` and does not run them. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-explain-this-code` may run from any lane, any time. It is not `/crav1-explain-existing-system`. It writes nothing into the repo unless the user picks Save as .md, and then only outside the repo. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-retire-spec` may run from any lane, on one spec the user names. Choice words are `retire`, `merge`, `park`, and `convert to note`. It runs no other skill. Parked specs are skipped by `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-build-features`, and the push branches of `/crav1-ado-sync`. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this` may run from any lane when the user asks about one feature, slice, or resource. With no report word it writes nothing in the project. A `report-*` word other than `report-data-model-full` writes one report outside the project. `report-data-model-full` writes under `docs/data-model/<model>/reviews/` and does not edit the saved model. No slice: it names a starter and does not run it. Pasted minutes name `/crav1-add-to-spec` and stop. It does not run another skill and does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-model-data` may run from any lane when the user asks for a data model. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not edit spec requirements, generate schema, or start a watcher. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs` may run from any lane. It runs `/crav1-add-to-spec` for each item and does not replace it. It does not run `/crav1-review-pr` or `/crav1-pr-status`. It does not commit. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build` may run from any lane when the user asks to tighten and plan a spec until it is ready to build. It is a guided walk, not a new lane and not a starter option. Asking for startup options names only the six and does not run this command. It runs the existing Specify and Plan skills inside the walk and does not replace them. It does not start Build, and it does not run `/crav1-build-tasks` or `/crav1-build-walk`. When the slice is ready, or ready-partial with tasks that can start, the ending recommends `/crav1-build-walk` and names `/crav1-build-tasks` as the alternative for one task without the walk. Since 1.150.0 that recommendation is a Run next block first. Each command is a complete invocation for a new session, and the reply prints each held line.

`/crav1-refresh-system-notes` may run from any lane, on its own. It adds what is new to the picture. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build, and it does not design or build the change. `/crav1-build-features`, `/crav1-fix-bug`, `/crav1-fix-build-gaps`, `/crav1-read-environment`, and `/crav1-add-to-spec` may ask whether to run it and do not run it. `/crav1-build-tasks` does not ask. It does not commit.

`/crav1-map-pipeline-environments` may run from any lane when the user names Azure DevOps, the org, and the project. It does not guess, and it does not run a pipeline. It names `/crav1-read-environment` and does not run it. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-review-security` may run from any lane, and only after architecture already exists. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. Spark, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-glossary` may run from any lane. With no word it shows the glossary and writes nothing. It never writes an open question onto a spec. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build, and it does not commit.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Suggest Features) may run from any lane. It lists Feature candidates and does not call Azure Boards. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Push Features) may run from any lane. It creates or updates a Feature only after a yes. A preview edit goes into the spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec` first. It names `/crav1-finalize-commit` and does not run it. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Push tasks) may run from any lane. It creates or updates a child of the Feature only after a yes. It names `/crav1-finalize-commit` and does not run it, and it names pull as the later read-back. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Pull tasks) may run from any lane. Kept changes go in through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. It never writes a field to Azure Boards. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Pull spec changes) may run from any lane. A kept change goes through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. A no-spec-yet Feature names a starter and does not run it. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-run-exploratory-test` may run from any lane, after a build of a slice already exists. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build, and it does not start those lanes. A bug it finds is not sent to `/crav1-fix-bug` unless the user says so in that turn. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-suggest-tests-for-code` may run from any lane when the user points at code that already exists. A kept suggestion goes onto the existing spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. It does not write the tests, change the code, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

Research is a cross-cutting helper with no slash command. Flag it when a run hits a technical question that needs research before Specify or Plan can proceed: choosing a technology or service, changing the architecture, scaling or modernizing, or judging an idea nobody has built yet.

Any lane that hits this flags it to the process orchestrator or guild lead, who pauses that lane and sends the researcher the question, the product or feature slug, and any constraints.

The researcher may use `/crav1-existing-to-specs` for parts the specs, plans, and code do not cover, and does not hand-edit those files. The researcher writes `docs/research/<topic>.md` (recommendation, trade-offs, confidence, and a link to the full study) and a `## Research findings` line that names that path. The kit's skills read `docs/research/` and `## Research findings`. No skill reads a `research.md` inside a spec folder. The researcher returns the recommendation to the process orchestrator or guild lead with a suggested lane. That role routes it. Aside from that note and that line, the researcher does not edit specs, plans, or code, and does not change the lane.

When a note in `docs/research/` is updated, the skill that writes it follows `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/research-stale-clear.md`. So do `/crav1-add-to-spec` and `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` when the user points that command at the file. `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` re-checks a point when the open question it was waiting on is answered. It does not commit.

## Recommended option

Every question with options that has a recommendation lists that option first and ends its label with ` (Recommended)`. The question text does not also say `Recommendation: X`. The shared rule is `docs/reference/question-cards.md`.

## Choice words for bots and scripted runs

The merged skills take exact choice words instead of `--flags`. A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking, for a person, a bot, or a headless run. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words; it does not guess. Runners should always pass the word.

| Skill | Question | Words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | What to read | `repos only` · `repos and bundle` |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | What to write | `one spec` · `spec per feature` |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | Recheck existing specs (1.108.0) | `recheck` · `repos vs specs` |
| `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` | List (optional, never asked) | `detailed` · `apply` |
| `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` | Show or ask | `show` · `ask` |
| `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` | Channel after ask (optional) | `research` |
| `/crav1-record-approval` | Write the line | `accept` |
| `/crav1-add-to-spec` | What you have | `fact` · `dump` · `code change` · `meeting` · `mail` · `chat` |
| `/crav1-build-tasks` | Which tasks | `one task` · `range` · `all tasks` |
| `/crav1-build-tasks` | Branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-build-walk` | Do this step | `yes` · `stop` |
| `/crav1-build-walk` | Whose branch | `switch` · `own` |
| `/crav1-build-walk` | Pull request description | `edit description` |
| `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` | Which gaps | `verify gaps` · `live gaps` |
| `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` | Branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Commit or message | `commit` · `message only` · `commit now` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Base branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Pull | `pull` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Style | `crav1` · `git log` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Trailer hook | `strip trailers` · `keep trailers` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | Review a branch (optional, 1.80.0) | `branch` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | PR branches on disk older than the pull request | `fetch pr branches` · `use disk` · `stop pr review` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | The comment as posted | `comment posted` · `newest comment` · `skip comment record` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | Which pull request | `pr<n>` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | Your side (optional; picked from the PR author otherwise) | `as reviewer` · `as author` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | How much | `since last` · `no code` |
| `/crav1-merge-pr` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-merge-pr` | The PR record says not ready (1.97.0) | `anyway` |
| `/crav1-help` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-help` | What to do next (optional, never asked) | `todo` · `todo next` · `todo top N` |
| `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` | Show the build map? | `build-map` |
| `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-explain-this-code` | How deep | `what it does` · `what and why` · `teach the language` |
| `/crav1-retire-spec` | What to do | `retire` · `merge` · `park` · `convert to note` |

| `/crav1-glossary` | Which mode | `as-file` · `research` · `<term>` |
| `/crav1-ado-sync` | Which sync | `suggest features` · `push features` · `push tasks` · `pull tasks` · `pull spec changes` |

Example: `/crav1-ado-sync push tasks`, `/crav1-existing-to-specs repos and bundle spec per feature`.
